mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals economic weakness, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE rises by more than 0.5% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three months signals strong consumer demand, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when RSAFS shows sustained growth over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within a month signals supply chain disruptions, reducing corporate output and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when INDPRO declines by more than 2% within a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 8% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decline for two consecutive months, it signals a weakening labor market, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 8% and PAYEMS declines for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when UNRATE is above 8% and PAYEMS declines for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% month-over-month and real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter, it signals strong economic demand, boosting corporate earnings and leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% MoM and GDPC1 grows > 2% QoQ
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST increases by more than 5% MoM and GDPC1 grows by more than 2% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% month-over-month and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2%, it signals inflationary pressure and tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of instances when CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% MoM and FEDFUNDS is above 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over three months signals a weakening supply chain, reducing corporate output and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO declines by more than 1% over three months.
